articles.content: Ella Langley won nearly every award she was up for, including the top prize, as well as female vocalist and album, single and song of the year. Stephen Wilson Jr. was a surprise to many in being named best new artist. Taylor Swift sang her nominated song and presented a lifetime achievement award to Brooks & Dunn. In a near-sweep that surprised no one, Ella Langley won six trophies at the CMA Awards , including the top prize, entertainer of the year. That’s an all-time record for the most awards ever won in a year by one person. The “Choosin’ Texas” singer so swept the field that the show’s host, Lainey Wilson , came out with a broom during her final acceptance speech and pretended to be cleaning up the stage. “I watched these awards since i was a little kid, and the awards i cared most about were song of the year and entertainer of the year,” Langley said at the close. Ultimately, after five turns at the podium (the sixth award was announced pre-telecast), she said, “I’ve run out of things to say. I’m at a loss for words.” But, she finally added, “I could quit tomorrow and have the best year of my life.” Langley came in to the show with a leading nine nominations. It was only possible for her to win seven, since she was nominated against herself in two categories (single and song of the year, where “Choosin’ Texas” had “Be Her” as competition). She wound up winning almost everything she could have, with the lone exception of a nomination she shared for musical event of the year. Her sweep of the other six possible categories included wins for best female vocalist; album of the year for “Dandelion”; and, for her record-breaking “Choosin’ Texas,” a triple crown of single of the year, song of the year and music video of the year. Desire, Death, and a Breakthrough Year for Queer Cinema

Desire, Death, and a Breakthrough Year for Queer Cinema
articles.content: A willingness to die for sex is a familiar bargain for queer people. Born in the twentieth century at the wrong place and time? Beware of Nazis, AIDS, and other mortal dangers. Hollywood has at times depicted these threats in ways that emphasize the humanity of LGBTQ+ people, as when Tom Hanks played a lawyer dying of AIDS in “Philadelphia,” during the height of the epidemic in 1993. The industry also has a history of finding ever more creative ways to kill off and scapegoat queer characters, a trope that as recently as 10 years ago seemed to be running amok . But a more twisted and nervy dance between desire and death has unfolded in this year’s spate of particularly macabre queer films. After years of what felt like permanent advances in rights and representation, LGBTQ+ people have been stung by backlash , including attacks on gender-affirming care, legal threats to marriage equality, and cuts to suicide prevention. Amid a reduced perception of safety , anxieties about the possibilities and consequences of nonnormative desire are spilling out onscreen like so much fake blood. Even so, their formulation is evidence of social and creative progress. articles.title: Larry Poindexter Dies: ‘S.W.A.T.’, ‘JAG’ & ‘Days Of Our Lives’ Actor Was 66
articles.content: Larry Poindexter , a veteran character actor who has appeared in almost 200 movies and TV series, passed away today, Nov. 18, four and a half days after being hit by a car. He was 66. Poindexter was struck while crossing the street to pick up food in his Studio City neighborhood Friday night. He had been at the hospital and scheduled to have a surgery for broken ribs today when he died suddenly this morning. Poindexter, whose career spanned more than four decades, is known for his role in the 2003 film S.W.A.T. in which he played by-the-book LAPD Captain Tom Fuller, who went head-to-head with Samuel Jackson’s Hondo. On TV, Poindexter appeared in 30 episodes of daytime drama Days Of Our Lives , playing two different characters, first in 1984 as Ben Welch, and as Father Louis from 2014-2018. He also did a 23-episode stint on Santa Barbara and 12 episodes of General Hospital . In primetime, Poindexter was a series regular on the MTV comedy series The Hard Times of RJ Berger and had a major recurring role on CBS’ JAG . He was a guest star on dozens of shows over the years, including playing Sergeant Boyer in the S.W.A.T. TV series and appearing in episodes of Quantum Leap, NYPD Blue, How I Met Your Mother, Friends, NCIS, Will & Grace, Scandal, CSI, CSI: Miami, CSI: NY, Party of Five, Nip/Tuck, Melrose Place, Weeds, Californication, Hawaii Five-0, Castle, Curb Your Enthusiasm, Supernatural, Bones, All Rise, Station 19, The Rookie, and 9-1-1. His most recent guest appearance was in Season 4 of The Lincoln Lawyer earlier this year. Also a musician, Poindexter was lead singer for the alternative country band The High Lonesome in the 1990s. Their album Feel Free To Do So was released in 1995. Poindexter is survived by his wife, leading casting director Carol Kritzer, and their two sons. Larry was as good as they come. He was one of the first people I met when I moved here decades ago, and remained a close friend. I know a lot of us felt that way: that he was a close friend.

articles.title: Willa, Women Make Movies Team to Release Shalini Kantayya’s Doc ‘Love Apptually’ Theatrically
articles.content: Willa and Women Make Movies have teamed up to distribute documentary “ Love Apptually ,” theatrically in the U.S. Set for a February released timed to Valentine’s Day, “Love Apptually,” directed by Shalini Kantayya, follows French journalist Judith Duportail’s journey from her early fascination with Tinder to an investigation into the technologies and business incentives mediating our search for human connection. After uncovering Tinder’s hidden desirability rating system, Duportail demanded access to her personal data, ultimately receiving 800 pages of information collected by the platform. What begins as a personal curiosity evolves into a global investigation into how a multi-billion-dollar tech industry is quietly reshaping desire, intimacy and love. Kantayya digs into how dating platforms are designed to maximize engagement and profit, often at the expense of authentic human connection. The film raises questions about agency, autonomy, privacy, and the commercialization of human intimacy. “I’ve watched Big Tech move from capturing our attention to shaping our most intimate human relationships. ‘Love Apptually’ asks whether the loneliness epidemic is a consequence of technological design,” said director Shalini Kantayya. The film bowed at Hot Docs and also recently screened at DOC NYC. “Love Apptually” marks the final installment in Kantayya’s trilogy examining technology’s impact on human experience, following “Coded Bias” and “TikTok, Boom.,” which both premiered at Sundance, screened on PBS’s Independent Lens and received Emmy nominations. “Valentine’s Day is a time when we celebrate love, but ‘Love Apptually’ asks us to look more closely at the forces shaping how we find it,” said Elizabeth Woodward, founder and CEO of Willa and producer of the film. “Shalini has created a film that reveals how technology has moved beyond capturing our attention to influencing our most intimate relationships. articles.content: Screen Gems has cleaned house, laying off a majority of its staff as the Sony division enters a new era under its incoming head, former YouTube executive Fede Goldenberg. The division, which specializing in genre movies such as Resident Evil and Underworld and comedies such as Easy A , has let go of senior vp Nathan Samdalh, vp Ellie Walker, and creative exec Peyton Collins, among others, sources tell The Hollywood Reporter . Goldenberg made the cuts and is expected to bring in a new team as he takes Screen Gems in a new direction. The exec was hired in early October and is bringing in a decidedly 2026 focus to the label. Under the new creative strategy, the film label is expanding its longstanding focus on traditional genre films to include theatrical projects from the next generation of so called “digital-native storytellers,” meaning filmmakers who are making names — and gaining followers — in the digital content space à la Curry Barker of Obsession fame and Backrooms filmmaker Kane Parsons. Goldenberg is expected to bring a new team with new roles to implement his digital creator-focused strategy. Ashley Brucks, who had been running the label as president since 2023 , transitioned to a producing role. Samdahl is the former Paramount executive who was instrumental in making the horror hit Smile (and was infamously let go from the studio before the movie became a surprise hit). He also acted as a creative exec at Walter Hamada’s production banner 18hz Productions. He joined Screen Gems in October 2025. Walker was also a former Paramount exec. articles.title: Sharon Horgan to Be the Guest of Honor at CanneSeries Industry
articles.summary: The TV industry event called the creator, writer and star of 'Catastrophe,' 'Bad Sisters' and 'Youth,' an "iconic voice" of TV and "undoubtedly one of the wittiest and funniest of our time."
articles.content: Irish actress, writer and producer Sharon Horgan will be the guest of honor at the 2027 CanneSeries Industry, the international TV event held alongside the CanneSeries television festival, organizers announced Tuesday. CanneSeries called Horgan, a BAFTA winner and Emmy nominee for her work on such series as Catastrophe , Divorce and Bad Sisters , an “iconic voice” of international TV and “undoubtedly one of the wittiest and funniest of our time.” In a statement, Albin Lewi and Claire-Marine Pietriga, artistic director and deputy artistic director of CanneSeries praised Horgan for her “sharp writing, dark humor and unflinching portrayal of human relationships,” noting her ability to “seamlessly blend comedy and drama, bringing to life complex, flawed and deeply authentic female characters.” Related Stories Movies European Lifetime Achievement Award for the Dardenne Brothers Music Harry Styles, Billie Eilish and Sam Fender Set to Headline Glastonbury 2027 As the co-founder of the production company Merman, they added “she continues to push the boundaries of television storytelling, championing bold narratives driven by strong female perspectives.” Horgan will attend CanneSeries Industry and will take part in its “meet with the participants” program to reflect on the key milestones of her career. The third edition of CanneSeries Industry will be held from Feb. 15-17 alongside the 10th CanneSeries festival, which runs Feb. 12-17. CanneSeries was initially a Spring event, held alongside the now-defunct TV trade fair MIPTV. It is shifting to February next year, putting it ahead of rival French TV event Series Mania, which runs March 19-26.

articles.content: The 60th annual Country Music Awards return this week, and they’re marking the milestone with some massive performances. Among them? None other than Taylor Swift , making her first appearance at the show in 13 years. She’s nominated for her song “I Knew It, I Knew You,” from “Toy Story 5.” So, how can Swifties ensure they don’t miss it? The 2026 CMAs will take place live at the Bridgestone Arena in Nashville on Wednesday, Nov. 18 at 8 p.m. ET. You’ve got a couple of options on this one. If you’d like to watch the awards show via the cable broadcast, you can tune into ABC . If you’d prefer to stream it, you can do that on Disney+. The show will also be available next day on Hulu. Lainey Wilson will host the CMAs this year, marking her third time hosting the event. As always, the CMAs will feature performances from country music favorites. This year, that includes Luke Combs, Vince Gill, Megan Moroney, Mumford & Sons, Chris Stapleton, Lainey Wilson, Stephen Wilson Jr. and more. But, one of the biggest performances of the night will come from the one and only Taylor Swift, who last appeared on the show more than a decade ago. Swift is nominated this year for Single of the Year with “ I Knew It, I Knew You ,” from “Toy Story 5,” marking her 26th career CMA nomination.

articles.summary: Exclusive: Set in New Jersey, Stephanie Ahn’s magical Sundance winner co-stars Son Sukku.
articles.content: The last person Audrey (Moon Choi) wants to share a ride with is Eli (Son Sukku), the other driver in her mother’s car accident. But when the New York physical therapist returns to her childhood home in New Jersey to care for her suddenly injured parent (Won Mi Kyung), Audrey finds herself carpooling with the local security guard — now without a car of his own. Somewhere along the way, she and Eli start looking forward to their next argument. And part of the fun of Stephanie Ahn’s stunning debut, “ Bedford Park ,” is wondering which of them will catch on first. Premiering exclusively on IndieWire, the film ’s official trailer offers a tantalizing glimpse at the buzzy Korean American romance Sony Pictures Classics acquired out of Sundance this past January . “ Bedford Park ” won the festival’s U.S. Dramatic Special Jury Award for Debut Feature and later screened at Toronto and Busan. articles.title: ‘I Play Rocky’ Star P.J. Byrne Isn’t a Scene-Stealer — He’s Something Better
articles.summary: A master of "hey, I love that guy!" roles, Byrne brings his usual gusto, good humor, and deep work ethic to the role of legendary producer Irwin Winkler. The result? As he tells IndieWire, "the most grounded performance" of his career, but with the "biggest laughs" yet. Perfect.
articles.content: You might not always remember his name, but you know P.J. Byrne . A master of “hey, I love that guy!” roles, the actor is often classified as a scene-stealer, thanks to standout turns in everything from “The Wolf of Wall Street” and “Babylon” to “Coyote vs. Acme” and “The Rainmaker.” Byrne is funny, yes , but also energetic and an eager scene partner. He improves his projects not by simply showing up and grabbing some quick guffaws, but by really doing the work, learning his characters inside and out, and making it a priority to truly understand his directors. In his own words, he’s not stealing scenes; he’s elevating them. He doesn’t ever want to be the best thing in a film or show — he wants his process to help everything be better. articles.title: Skydance to Combine Warner Bros. Television Group and Paramount Television Studios as One Big Studio
articles.summary: Channing Dungey and Matt Thunell will team up to lead the combined group.
articles.content: The corporate shakeups keep coming at Skydance , this time to the TV department. Warner Bros. Television Group and Paramount Television Studios are being combined as one big studio under Skydance , with WB’s Channing Dungey and Paramount’s Matt Thunell serving as presidents of the combined studio. The new studio, which officially launches in early 2027 (the two entities will keep operating independently until then), will be known as Warner Bros. Television Studios. The entire studio will report to George Cheeks, co-chair and Chief Content Officer of Skydance TV. As previously announced, Dungey also serves as Chair of Skydance Global Cable Media, with oversight over all 50+ WB Discovery and Paramount cable brands. articles.summary: Scott vividly portrays "Gandhi" and "Chariots of Fire" star Ian Charleson, who made "Hamlet" his final role at the National Theatre, but the movie around him sinks into forgettability.
articles.content: [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on September 5, 2026 during the 2026 Telluride Film Festival. Focus Features will release the film in theaters Friday, November 20.] There’s no question Andrew Scott , the 49-year-old Irish actor, has earned his position as one of the finest contemporary actors going. He’s in demand, but choosing wisely, and in roles that slyly play off his own status as an out gay man (a rare thing indeed) but with something off-center beneath, often a secret. He played Tom Ripley, one even more sociopathic than Matt Damon’s own iconically calculating Adonis, to devastating effect in the sinister Netflix series “ Ripley ,” there more explicitly grappling with the Patricia Highsmith character’s ambiguous (but was it?) sexuality. He played the Hot Priest who turned down a chance at heterosexual, secular love in “Fleabag,” of course, and starred in “All of Us Strangers” as a lonely adult orphan living in a glittering tower, bracing himself for romantic intimacy with Paul Mescal. And Universal is hoping that audiences will turn out for a healthy dose of celebrity schadenfreude. Judd Apatow ‘s new film stars Glen Powell as a rising country superstar who happens to be dating the world’s biggest pop icon (Madelyn Cline). articles.summary: A tough and unflinching social drama about the predators among us — and how difficult it can be to see them for what they are.
articles.content: [Editor’s note: This review was originally published on May 15, 2026 during the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. Netflix will release the film on its streaming platform on Wednesday, November 18.] Marie Kreutzer ’s “ Gentle Monster ” opens with virtuoso musician Lucy Weiss ( Léa Seydoux ) sitting at the piano in her Munich apartment and plunking out a stilted but affecting cover of Charles & Eddie’s neo-soul classic “Would I Lie to You?” This is before her Austrian husband Philip (Laurence Rupp) — a documentary TV producer of marginal success — comes home in a burnout panic that spurs them to permanently relocate their family to a cottage in the German countryside. Before the authorities bang on their door with a warrant for Philip’s arrest, forcing Lucy to ride the elevator up to the clearly designated “child porn” floor of the local police station in order to learn the facts of his case. Before she begins to wonder, in rage and terror and desperate layers of self-protective doubt, whether the father of her young son Johnny (Malo Blanchet) might actually be capable of preying on other kids, or even his own. articles.summary: In October, the Tehran Revolutionary Court sentenced Jafar Panahi to more than five years in prison, plus additional penalties such as the seizure of assets and the freezing of his bank accounts.
articles.content: The film community is marshaling to support Oscar-nominated, dissident Iranian filmmaker Jafar Panahi , who was given a prison sentence of five years and one month by the Tehran Revolutionary Court back in October . A letter initiated by the International Coalition for Filmmakers at Risk ( and shared with Variety ) so far features more than 200 signatories “deeply concerned by reports of the new prison sentence of five years and one month issued by the Tehran Revolutionary Court against Iranian filmmaker Jafar Panahi , in absentia.” Panahi returned to Iran in the spring following the end of Neon’s awards run for his Cannes Film Festival Palme d’Or winner “It Was Just an Accident,” nominated for Best International Feature and Best Original Screenplay at the 2026 Academy Awards. Festival leaders who signed the letter include Berlinale director Tricia Tuttle, New York Film Festival artistic director Dennis Lim, Venice’s Alberto Barbera, Telluride head Julie Huntsinger, and others — many of whom have hosted Panahi’s films across the last four decades. Previously, Panahi was sentenced to one year in prison and a two-year ban on leaving Iran in December, in absentia. articles.title: What Happens If We Break Letterboxd?
articles.summary: Repertory theaters have been a bright spot in a rough stretch for Hollywood. A possible Letterboxd sale raises concerns about how old movies find new audiences — and what happens if those young cinephiles scatter.
articles.content: Earlier this month, the Trylon in Minneapolis gave audiences six chances over three days to see “Kanał,” Andrzej Wajda’s 1957 film about Polish resistance fighters retreating into the sewers of Warsaw. After opening night, programmer John Moret saw enthusiastic reviews on Letterboxd . Moret could imagine the calculation for somebody still on the fence: “Oh, these people I trust went to go see this movie, and they loved it. And it’s just playing for two more days.” On November 5, the New York Times reported that its parent company was in exclusive talks to buy Letterboxd for roughly $330 million. Under the deal being discussed, the popular film-logging site would likely keep operating on its own but use the Times Company’s advertising technology. Related Stories How GKIDS Home Releases Are Creating the Fandom They Want to See in the World IDA Documentary Awards 2026 Nominations: ‘You Can See Everything,’ ‘Concrete Land,’ and More Earn Nods For theaters like the Trylon, what matters is whether cinephiles who went on opening night can still reach those who might go tomorrow. In 2026, that handoff is working remarkably well on Letterboxd. Five days before “Kanał” opened, Ken Russell’s “The Devils” sold out at the Trylon on election night . Moret also co-founded the national Programmers’ Jam with Bret Berg, theatrical sales director at the American Genre Film Archive, and Dan Halsted of Portland’s Hollywood Theatre. When the Jam met in Los Angeles in May, Berg told IndieWire that programmers had access to more restorations than ever before; plus, more places to show them and a new audience coming through the doors. We helped declare it the Golden Age of Repertory programming this spring. articles.content: Specialists at IDFA discussed the dos-and-dont's of licensing material to AI training machines as the practice becomes more common among rights holders Back in 2024, leading documentary film festival IDFA opened with Piotr Winiewicz’s “About a Hero,” a documentary that set out to test the premise of whether or not an AI model could conceive a Werner Herzog film. Back then, the film received some backlash for its use of the technology, with docmakers— including Herzog —openly rebuffing the use of artificial intelligence in cinema. Like the technology itself, much has changed in terms of discussions around AI in the two years since, with more and more industry experts admitting to not only using AI in their films but also willingly feeding the training systems. Recently, lauded filmmaker Ava DuVernay admitted to using AI in Netflix doc “14th” to animate public-domain archival photographs and bring historical periods to life.
